outputs.exact_statement: There exist a vocabulary $\tau$ of eight binary relations, a fixed polynomial $p$, and a $\mathrm{CPT}+\mathrm{WSC}$ sentence $(\Phi,p)$ with one occurrence of a WSC operator such that:* 1. *$(\Phi,p)$ has a Boolean value on every finite $\tau$-structure;* 2. *no $\mathrm{CPT}$ sentence over $\tau$ has the same true-model class.* *The $\mathrm{CPT}$ sentences in (ii) may use counting and hereditarily finite sets of unrestricted finite rank.

For every $L\ge2$ and $b\in\mathbb F_3^{V_L}$, the maps $h_{a,k}$ define a faithful action of $H$ by automorphisms of the entire $\tau$-structure $A_b$. Every $h_{a,k}$ preserves each edge and configuration block setwise. For $k\in K$, the central action $h_{0,k}$ fixes all face vectors and adds $k_e$ to the scalar coordinate on edge $e$.

Suppose $\operatorname{Check}(A)$ holds, $\alpha\in P$, and $\operatorname{Complete}(\alpha,x)$ holds. Then $\Phi_{\rm out}(\alpha,x)$ is true if and only if there exist atoms $t_v\in v$, for every $v\in\mathcal V$, and $s_e\in e$, for every $e\in\mathcal E$, such that $$\mathsf I(t_v,s_e)\quad\text{whenever }v\sim e,
 \qquad s_e\in x\quad\text{whenever }e\notin T.$$

For every input and every $\alpha\in P$, each choice set reached from $x=\emptyset$ is a nonempty orbit under the automorphisms fixing $\alpha$ and every preceding state. The corresponding value of $s_{\rm wit}$ witnesses that orbit using automorphisms of the full input. Every path reaches its first repeated state after at most $n+1$ transitions.

For every finite input, the expansion of Equation [sen:sentence], annotated by Equation [sen:polynomial], has the following properties. Every constructed set, including temporary sets before any filtering, has transitive size at most $p(n)$. Every ordinary iteration stabilizes within $p(n)$ steps, and every WSC path to first stabilization has at most $p(n)$ state labels.

The sentence $(\Phi,p)$ of Equations [sen:sentence] and [sen:polynomial] is a fixed $\mathrm{CPT}+\mathrm{WSC}$ sentence over $\tau$. It evaluates to either true or false on every finite $\tau$-structure, never to $\dagger$, and its true-model class is isomorphism-invariant.* *More explicitly, it is true precisely when $P\ne\emptyset$ and there exists $\alpha\in P$ such that every terminal state of the guarded selection is complete and extends to consistent configurations as in Lemma 5.
Every structure $A_b$ passes the input check of Section 4, its block graph is the box on $V_L$, and its parameter set $P$ is nonempty.

Let $A_b$ be a grid structure, $\alpha\in P$, and $x$ a compatible prefix of length $j<r$. For every ordered pair $s,s'\in D(\alpha,x)$ there is $g\in M(\alpha,x)$ with $g(s)=s'$. The map $g$ preserves the full input, fixes every block setwise, and fixes every atom of $x$ individually. Consequently every selection path for $\alpha$ chooses one atom from each edge outside $T$, in order, maintains compatibility, and then stabilizes with the dummy choice. All its witnessing maps respect $\alpha$ and the entire preceding history.

Let $T$ be a finite tree on vertex set $V$, orient its edges arbitrarily, and write $\partial_T$ for its signed incidence map. Let $r\in\mathbb F_3^V$ satisfy $\sum_{v\in V}r_v=0$. There is a unique $z\in\mathbb F_3^{E(T)}$ with $\partial_T z=r$.

For every $L\ge2$, the fixed sentence $\Phi$ of Section 4 evaluates to true on $A_{b^0}$ and to false on $A_{b^1}$. For either structure, every parameter $\alpha\in P$ and every terminal selection gives the stated output value, and no evaluation produces $\dagger$.

Let $\ell\in\mathbb F_3^E$, and let $t=|\{f\in F:(D\ell)(f)\ne0\}|$. There is a vertex function $\varphi\in\mathbb F_3^V$ such that $$|\operatorname{supp}(\ell-\partial^{\mathsf T}\varphi)|\le2Lt,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{supp}(r)=\{e\in E:r_e\ne0\}.$$ In particular, every cochain with zero curl is a gradient.

Let $L\ge2$, $b\in\mathbb F_3^{V_L}$, and $N=|A_b|$. Let $q\ge0$ and let $x$ be an atom or a hereditarily finite set over $A_b$. If $|H\cdot x|\le N^q$, then $x$ has a $K$-support consisting of at most $$2L(q\log_3N)^2$$ edge atoms. There is no bound on the finite rank of $x$ in this statement.

Let $L\ge2$, $b\in\mathbb F_3^{V_L}$, and $N=|A_b|$. Suppose $\mathcal X$ is a finite $H$-invariant, membership-transitive family of atoms and hereditarily finite sets over $A_b$, with $|\mathcal X|\le N^q$ for some $q\ge0$. Every member of $\mathcal X$ and every recursive member has a $K$-support of length at most $2L(q\log_3N)^2$. In particular, every member is hereditarily $s$-supported for $$\label{sup:length}
 s=\left\lceil2L(q\log_3N+1)^2\right\rceil+1.$$ All the supports may be padded to length exactly $s$. For fixed $q$, $$s=O_q\bigl(L(1+\log L)^2\bigr).$$
Let $c=1-2^{-1/3}$. For every $L\ge2$ and every nonempty $R\subseteq\{0,\ldots,L-1\}^3$ with $|R|\le L^3/2$, $$|\delta_G R|\ge c|R|^{2/3}.$$

For all sufficiently large $L$, every graph $G\setminus T$ obtained by deleting at most $6M$ edges has a unique component with more than $L^3/2$ vertices. If $T\subseteq T'$ and $|T'|\le6M$, the component for $T'$ is contained in the component for $T$.
For all sufficiently large $L$, the expansions $\bar A_{b^0}$ and $\bar A_{b^1}$ satisfy the same $C^M$ sentences, where $b^0=0$, $b^1=\mathbf1_{v_*}$, and $M$ is as in [base:M].

Let $L\ge2$, $b\in\mathbb F_3^V$, and let $r,M$ be positive integers such that $$\label{base:homogeneity-bound}
 7r+7(6r/c)^{3/2}+1\le M.$$ If two $r$-tuples in $\bar A_b$ have the same $C^M$-type, an element of $K$ maps the first tuple to the second. Empty tuples lie in the same $K$-orbit without any width hypothesis.

Fix positive integers $q,m$ independently of $L$, and let $$N=N_L=\Theta(L^3),\qquad s=\left\lceil2L(q\log_3N+1)^2\right\rceil+1, \qquad M=\lfloor L^{7/4}\rfloor.$$ For all sufficiently large $L$, Proposition 20 holds, Proposition 22 applies to every tuple length $1\le r\le(m+4)s$ in either expansion, and $$\max\{4,m+1\}s\le M.$$ In particular, both expansions are $K$-homogeneous for equal $C^M$ types of tuples of length at most $\max\{2,m\}s$.

Let $B_0,B_1$ be nonempty finite structures in the same finite relational vocabulary of arity at most two, and let $K_i\leq\operatorname{Aut}(B_i)$ for $i=0,1$. Let $s,m,M$ be positive integers with $$\max\{4,m+1\}s\leq M.$$ Suppose that:*

1.  *$B_0$ and $B_1$ satisfy the same $C^M$ sentences;*

2.  *in each $B_i$, any two tuples of length at most $\max\{2,m\}s$ having the same $C^M$ type belong to the same $K_i$-orbit.*

*Then $D_s(B_0,K_0)$ and $D_s(B_1,K_1)$ satisfy the same $C^m$ sentences in membership, atomhood, and the base relations.

Let $P,P'$ be tuples of the same length $a$, in two structures chosen from $B_0,B_1$, allowing the two structures to be the same. Suppose that $P,P'$ have the same $C^M$ type. If $a+d\leq M$, then for every realized type $\rho$ of length $a+d$, the numbers of tuples $\gamma,\gamma'$ of length $d$ satisfying $$\operatorname{tp}_M(P,\gamma)=\rho,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{tp}_M(P',\gamma')=\rho$$ are equal. Equal types also give equal types on every projected or reordered subtuple.
Every value $\phi*\alpha$ lies in $D_i$ and is supported by $\alpha$. Every object of $D_i$ has a representation of this kind. Furthermore, for each $g\in K_i$, $$g(\phi*\alpha)=\phi*(g\alpha).$$

Let $\phi,\psi$ be forms, and let $(\alpha,\beta)$ and $(\alpha',\beta')$ be pairs of molecules having the same $C^M$ type, in the same or different base structures. Then $$\begin{aligned}
 \phi*\alpha=\psi*\beta
   &\ \Longleftrightarrow\
       \phi*\alpha'=\psi*\beta',\\
 \phi*\alpha\in\psi*\beta
   &\ \Longleftrightarrow\
       \phi*\alpha'\in\psi*\beta'.
\end{aligned}$$ Atomhood and all base relations also agree on the corresponding values.

For represented-alike assignments with $r\leq m-1$, there is a bijection $f:D_0\to D_1$ such that adjoining $x,f(x)$ gives represented-alike assignments for every $x\in D_0$. Moreover, $f(x_j)=x'_j$ for every retained position $j$.

For every fixed CPT sentence $\psi$, there is an integer $q\ge1$ such that, on every sufficiently large finite input $A$ of size $n$, $$|\mathcal T_\psi(A)|\le n^q.$$ The family $\mathcal T_\psi(A)$ is membership-transitive and invariant under $\operatorname{Aut}(A)$. It includes the first excessive candidate of each activated iteration and, when needed, its candidate at index $P(n)+1$.

Fix a CPT sentence $\psi$. There are an integer $m\ge1$ and, for each sufficiently large input size $n$, a $C^m$ sentence $\widehat\psi_n$ with the following property.*

*Let $A$ be an $n$-element input and let $D\subseteq\operatorname{HF}(A)$ be membership-transitive, contain all atoms and all pure HF sets, and contain $\mathcal T_\psi(A)$. Interpret membership and the atom predicate on $D$, and interpret each input relation as false if an argument is a set. Then $$D\models\widehat\psi_n
       \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \psi\text{ evaluates to true on }A.$$ The formula $\widehat\psi_n$ depends only on $\psi$ and $n$, not on $A$ or $D$. Its length and counting constants may depend on $n$; $m$ does not.

For every sentence $\psi$ of full CPT with counting over $\tau$, there is $L_\psi$ such that for every $L\ge L_\psi$, $$A_{b^0}\models\psi
       \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A_{b^1}\models\psi .$$

purpose: Witnessed symmetric choice is strictly stronger than choiceless polynomial time with counting

coverage.checked_domain: The listed finite trees with n <= 6, including the singleton, reversed orientations, a branching tree, zero demands, and nonzero zero-total demands; invalid total and graph hypotheses are also exercised.
coverage.oracle_basis: Exhaustive exact enumeration of all edge assignments verifies the unique solution on each valid vector. The singleton vector is index 0; the forward-edge vector is index 1; the propagation-path vector is index 3. These finite checks do not prove the universal lemma.
